subject: Re: Pegasus Ops — purge request: prompts, outputs, and per-request logs
messages:
From: Alan Park <alan.park@pegasus-ops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pegasus Ops (security) <security@pegasus-ops.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Purge request: prompts, outputs, per-request logging for project 'Tessera'

Marcus —

Thanks for the heads-up on onboarding. Pegasus has completed our internal retention review and we need Redwood to execute a one-time purge for the Tessera integration: all prompt inputs, assistant outputs, and per-request logs (including KV cache entries and transient traces) generated between 2028-04-01 and 2028-10-31. This is scoped to the Tessera project and the workspace id: ws-peg-77.

Request details:
- Scope: prompts, response outputs, request-level telemetry/logs, and any ephemeral KV cache slices associated with ws-peg-77.
- Time window: 2028-04-01 to 2028-10-31 (inclusive)
- Compliance need: Pegasus is doing an external audit and requires a purge certificate plus evidence of wipe (ops logs, runbook id, and any hash/snapshot of removed keys).

Attached is our intake form with signer details. Please confirm the expected timeline, what evidence we will receive, and whether any of this triggers escalation or affects their live throughput. We need to share the timeframe with our auditor by EOD Friday.

Best,
Alan Park
Security Operations
Pegasus Ops

Attachment: pegasus_purge_request_20281101.pdf (form)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Park <alan.park@pegasus-ops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purge request: prompts, outputs, per-request logging for project 'Tessera'

Alan —

Thanks for the clear scope and the intake PDF. We're able to run the purge under our normal customer deletion playbook. High level:

1) Intake & verification (today): ops will validate workspace id, data locations (hosted vs. dedicated), and whether any retained backups overlap the window.
2) Dry-run & snapshot (24–48 hours): create immutable evidence snapshots (ops-only), identify keys/objects to delete, and run a non-destructive verification.
3) Execution (48–72 hours after dry-run sign-off): perform deletion across prompt logs, model outputs, and request logs; purge eligible KV cache slices.
4) Post-run evidence & certificate (within 24 hours of execution): deliver a signed purge certificate, deletion manifest (list of object ids obfuscated), and ops runbook id.

Two quick clarifications we need before scheduling the dry-run:
- Is there any ongoing replay/retention job that uses ws-peg-77 snapshots? If yes, we need a skip-window or freeze.
- Do you require zeroization of derivable embeddings (we can either expunge embeddings for the window or keep them if you prefer anonymized retention)?

Marissa — can you pick this up on the ops side (confirm backups and give a proposed execution window)? Neha — can you confirm the audit artifacts we usually provide (hashes, runbook id format, and an ops-level timeline)?

If we get confirmation today, we can target execution by Friday evening PST.

—Marcus
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Alan Park <alan.park@pegasus-ops.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purge request: prompts, outputs, per-request logging for project 'Tessera'

Alan / Marcus —

I pulled the workspace metadata: ws-peg-77 is on our hosted multi-tenant cluster in us-west-2 (not Dedicated). Backups: nightly snapshots exist and retention policies for those snapshots extend 90 days beyond the request window; that means some snapshots overlap into November. Our standard procedure is to identify and delete snapshot deltas that contain the scoped objects, then update snapshot manifests.

Proposed timeline (assuming Alan signs off to proceed):
- 2028-11-02 09:00 PST: Dry-run (identify object ids, generate verification manifest).
- 2028-11-02 13:00 PST: Ops review & sign-off.
- 2028-11-02 16:00–20:00 PST: Execution window — deletion jobs across storage, request logs, and cache invalidation.
- 2028-11-03 08:00 PST: Post-run proof package delivered (certificate.pdf, deletion-manifest-obfuscated.csv, ops-log-trace.txt).

Evidence we will supply:
- Signed purge certificate (PDF)
- Deletion manifest (object ids obfuscated with deterministic salt)
- Ops runbook id: RB-20281102-PEG
- Execution traces: redwood-ops-trace-<timestamp>.txt (redacted where necessary)
- If requested: a notarized statement from our compliance team (additional lead-time).

Notes and choices for you:
- Embeddings: we can either fully zeroize embeddings derived from prompts in scope (recommended) or replace them with salted hashes (less destructive, might satisfy some auditors). Which do you prefer?
- Backup handling: we will remove the deltas containing the scoped records; full snapshot re-creation may be necessary for a few clients but we will minimize cluster impact.

Attachments: redaction-checklist.csv (internal ops checklist)

Please reply with a one-line "proceed" and your embedding preference.

—Marissa
Senior Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alan Park <alan.park@pegasus-ops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pegasus Ops (security) <security@pegasus-ops.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purge request: prompts, outputs, per-request logging for project 'Tessera'

Marissa / Marcus —

Proceed. We require full zeroization of embeddings for the window and the full evidence package you listed (certificate + obfuscated manifest + ops trace). If you can include the deterministic salt method used to obfuscate ids in the audit package (we'll keep the salt under seal), that will help our auditor reconcile.

Please proceed with the dry-run on 2028-11-02 as proposed. If anything unexpected appears during the dry-run that would delay execution beyond Friday evening PST, flag me immediately.

Thanks for quick coordination.

Regards,
Alan Park
Security Operations
Pegasus Ops
